nodes.title: Incompatible bounds: the reusable argument
assumptions: A real sequence xₖ is defined on the same infinite index sequence.
liminf xₖ > L; limsup xₖ < U; L ≥ U.
nodes.justification: For every real sequence, liminf xₖ ≤ limsup xₖ (allowing extended limits). The hypotheses would instead give liminf xₖ > L ≥ U > limsup xₖ. The lower limit cannot exceed the upper limit. This proves the conditional contradiction, not the estimates used to invoke it.
nodes.extraction: Curated proof contract. Dependency checks test declared structure only; no formal proof checker has been run.

nodes.title: Why liminf cannot exceed limsup
assumptions: xₖ is a real sequence.
nodes.justification: Let aₙ=inf{xₖ:k≥n} and bₘ=sup{xₖ:k≥m}. For any n,m, choose k≥max(n,m); then aₙ≤xₖ≤bₘ. Taking the supremum over n and then the infimum over m gives supₙ aₙ≤infₘ bₘ, the claimed inequality. Extended real bounds are allowed.

nodes.title: Catalan: rationality of the determinants
nodes.summary: Δ_N is rational for every positive integer N.
assumptions: Assume Catalan’s constant G is rational.
Use the manuscript’s specified determinant construction.
nodes.conclusion: Δ_N is rational for every positive integer N.
nodes.justification: The source states that each raw entry lies in ℚ+ℚG. Under the rationality assumption the entries, and hence their determinants, are rational. Establishing the claimed form of the entries remains part of the source proof.

nodes.title: prop:rationality
nodes.summary: Each raw entry $F_j(r)$ lies in $\mathbb Q+\mathbb QG$. Consequently, if $G\in\mathbb Q$, then $\Delta_N\in\mathbb Q$ for every positive integer $N$.

nodes.title: Catalan: determinants must be nonzero
nodes.summary: Δ_p ≠ 0 for every sufficiently large prime p.
assumptions: Assume G is rational.
Use the manuscript’s determinant construction at N=p, for sufficiently large primes p.
nodes.conclusion: Δ_p ≠ 0 for every sufficiently large prime p.
nodes.justification: The manuscript claims the exact finite valuation v_p(Δ_p)=−96p. A finite valuation entails nonzero Δ_p. The claimed valuation is not checked here.
nodes.extraction: Curated proof contract. Dependency checks test declared structure only; no formal proof checker has been run.

nodes.title: prop:nonvanishing
nodes.summary: Assume that $G\in\mathbb Q$. For every sufficiently large prime $p$, the determinant with scale parameter $N=p$ satisfies \begin{equation} v_p(\Delta_p)=-96p. \end{equation} In particular, $\Delta_p\ne0$ for every sufficiently large prime $p$.

nodes.title: Catalan: conditional lower bound
nodes.summary: Along sufficiently large primes, liminf x_p > −2.29084.
assumptions: Assume G is rational.
Δ_N ≠ 0 along the chosen infinite sequence.
Use the same Δ_N and n=48N as in the source.
nodes.conclusion: Along sufficiently large primes, liminf x_p > −2.29084.
nodes.justification: Set x_p=log|Δ_p|/(48p)²−(log 2)/2. The source finite-place estimate gives the lower bound when its rationality and nonzero hypotheses hold. A nonzero argument is necessary for a real logarithm. The finite-place estimate itself is unverified here.
nodes.extraction: Curated proof contract. Dependency checks test declared structure only; no formal proof checker has been run.

nodes.title: Finite-place bound
nodes.summary: Assume $G\in\mathbb Q$. Along any sequence of positive integers $N\to\infty$ for which $\Delta_N\ne0$, one has \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \left(\frac{\log|\Delta_N|}{n^2}-\frac12\log2\right) \ge -\frac{8609}{4608} -\left(\frac12+\frac{505}{4608}\right)\log2 >-2.29084. \end{equation}

nodes.title: Catalan: source upper bound
nodes.summary: Along that prime sequence, limsup x_p ≤ −2.290939875 < −2.2909.
assumptions: Use the same determinant construction and normalization.
Restrict to the same sufficiently large primes with nonzero determinants.
nodes.conclusion: Along that prime sequence, limsup x_p ≤ −2.290939875 < −2.2909.
nodes.justification: The source asserts an upper bound along the full index sequence. Restricting to a subsequence cannot increase the limsup. Its majorant and numerical certificate have not been rechecked here.
nodes.extraction: Curated proof contract. Dependency checks test declared structure only; no formal proof checker has been run.

nodes.title: prop:real-upper
nodes.summary: For the determinants of Equation~\eqref{eq:determinant}, \begin{equation} \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left(\frac{\log|\Delta_N|}{n^2} -\frac12\log2\right) \le -2.290939875<-2.2909. \end{equation} The separate bounds for the majorants in cases $\kappa=2$ and $\kappa=1$ are $-2.290939875$ and $-2.296789875$,…

nodes.title: Catalan: the proof’s final contradiction
nodes.summary: Conditional on the cited propositions, G cannot be rational.
assumptions: Assume G is rational for contradiction.
Accept all four cited source propositions, with their definitions and hypotheses.
nodes.conclusion: Conditional on the cited propositions, G cannot be rational.
nodes.justification: The two estimates concern the same sequence x_p. The lower threshold −2.29084 is greater than the upper threshold −2.2909 by 0.00006. The incompatible-bounds argument yields a contradiction. This is a shorter explanation of the final step, not a new proof of the source propositions or a verified resolution of the research problem.

nodes.title: Candidate: can we omit nonvanishing?
nodes.summary: Blocked: the lower-bound contract requires Δ_p ≠ 0.
assumptions: Try to retain the same lower-bound theorem.
Omit the nonvanishing proposition without providing a replacement.
nodes.conclusion: Blocked: the lower-bound contract requires Δ_p ≠ 0.
nodes.justification: Rationality does not imply nonzero: zero is rational. Without nonvanishing on an infinite subsequence, x_p need not be a real sequence and the lower-bound theorem is not applicable. A replacement must establish nonvanishing on an unbounded subsequence for which both estimates hold, or supply a different estimate with different hypotheses.

nodes.title: Sum formula by reversing the sum
assumptions: n is a positive integer.
nodes.justification: Write S again in reverse order: S=n+(n−1)+…+1. Add term by term. Each of the n pairs is n+1, so 2S=n(n+1). Divide by two. This is a direct argument using finite sums.
nodes.extraction: Curated proof contract. Dependency checks test declared structure only; no formal proof checker has been run.

nodes.title: Sum formula by induction
assumptions: n ranges over positive integers.
nodes.justification: Base: for n=1, 1=1·2/2. Step: assume the formula at n. Add n+1 to obtain n(n+1)/2+(n+1)=(n+1)(n+2)/2, the formula at n+1. Induction proves all positive cases.

nodes.title: Can the domain be changed to all real n?
nodes.summary: Blocked: “the first n positive integers” is not defined for arbitrary real n.
assumptions: Keep the same finite-sum statement.
Replace positive integer n by any real number.
nodes.conclusion: Blocked: “the first n positive integers” is not defined for arbitrary real n.
nodes.justification: The expression n(n+1)/2 has a real-valued extension. That does not extend the original finite-sum theorem without a new definition of the left-hand side. A changed statement needs its own assumptions and argument.
